newsitem.title: MEXICO: Analysts see Ahmsa on improving path.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Ahmsa on improving path.

text.p: New projects coming on line in 1997 should boost second quarter operations at Mexican steel company Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa), analysts said.

Nevertheless, earnings will appear weak as the peso's strength cut into the company's dollar-denominated sales. Three analysts surveyed by Reuters estimated earnings of 1.36 pesos per share, compared to 3.407 pesos per share in the year-ago period.
Analysts said that despite the Acrippling affect of Ahmsa's monetary position, the company has been working to improve efficiency and increase value-added products.
"I'm expecting a good report with a continuing tendency toward improved margins from modernization projects begun in 1996," Serfin brokerage's Yvonne Delgadillo said.

While new projects from a $975 million five-year plan have been coming on-line, Ahmsa has had to buy some materials from the outside, Delgadillo said. This raised their costs and consequently their operating margins.

Analysts estimated margins for the second three months of the year at about 17 percent, agreeing there would be a definite improvement from the 16.3 percent margins reported in the first quarter. Sales were estimated at between three billion and 3.5 billion pesos.
In the second quarter, Ahmsa's results were dragged down by steel prices at 40 percent below 1996 levels. Sales were also hurt by the peso's strength, industry observers said.

"We expect that 1998 will be a more favorable year because of the savings in costs, the normalization of operations and a smaller appreciation of the peso," Accival analysts Arturo Espinosa and Rafael Urquia wrote in a recent report.
Ahmsa said recently that it expected its new projects to gradually generate savings in energy and operation costs.

The company's new coal-injection system, scheduled to go on-line at the end of the year, will reduce energy costs to $2.11 per British Thermal Unit (BTU), compared with a previous $2.46 spent per BTU for natural gas.

Reducing bottlenecks at one of the company's coking plants will eliminate the outside purchasing of 159,000 tonnes of coke, at about $145 per tonne. The project, scheduled to be completed in the third quarter of 1998, will produce coke at a cost of $63 per tonne, Ahmsa said.
"I think that some of the benefit from the value-added projects you will see in the second quarter," Salomon Brothers' analyst Mauricio Reveco said.
Analysts projected Mexico's steel market would get a boost from the expected continuing improvement in Mexico's domestic market.
Reveco said Mexico's steel prices should follow Brazil's recent 14 to 18 percent hike.
An improved, but still heavy debt profile will continue to hold the company back however, analysts said.

"Ahmsa recently fixed up its debt in some transactions to improve its leverage. The company is still heavily indebted because of all the vertically integrated projects that make it one of the lowest cost steel companies in North America," Valores Finamex's Chris Albi said.
